items.title: India becomes the latest country to report rogue AI agent activity
items.snippet: The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles.

items.title: An Nvidia insider-turned-VC on why robotics hasn’t hit its ChatGPT moment, yet
items.snippet: Amulya Vishwanath, who spent seven years leading product marketing for NVIDIA’s robotics platforms, says robotics is currently in its “Lego era,” with the basic building blocks like actuators, robotic hands, software, and safety standards still being rebuilt. This view runs counter to those who believe that robotics, powered by a general foundation model, is about to have […]

items.title: Elorian’s first AI model wants to reason with images, not just about them
items.snippet: According to Elorian's evaluations, Glimpse outperforms even GPT-6 Astra on scientific chart reasoning and short-form video captioning, with competitive results on other visual reasoning tasks.

items.title: Tressfecta wants to make hair braiding a less arduous task for hairstylists
items.snippet: Tressfecta builds products for textured hair. Its first project is a tool called Plait Pilot that helps braiders with the initial process of separating hair from packs before braiding begins.

items.title: Jev is Vercel's fastest-adopted AI model ever
items.snippet: The data comes from Vercel's AI gateway, a unified API service similar to OpenRouter.

items.title: Mark Wahlberg on using AI in film 'the right way' and being open to an AI clone carrying on his legacy
items.snippet: Actor and angel investor Mark Wahlberg says he's OK with using AI in filmmaking, provided it's used "to enhance what you're doing."

items.title: Veritas expands its anti-counterfeit chip to jewelry, trophies, and fragrance bottles
items.snippet: Counterfeiters are getting better at replicating brands' marks and passing off dupes, known as "superfakes," as genuine items. A startup called Veritas wants to tackle the problem with its own chip that verifies goods.

items.title: Replit's CEO says the future of work is the 'self-driving company'
items.snippet: Replit CEO Amjad Masad envisions a future of “self-driving companies,” where AI agents handle day-to-day tasks and people focus on higher-level decisions.

items.title: Even Benchmark thinks AI is eroding the venture pact against backing rivals
items.snippet: Benchmark says the Valley’s rule against backing rivals is getting harder to keep.

items.title: Tesla reveals SpaceX-powered Roadster that flies and falls with style
items.snippet: The new car used thrusters to leap over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Tesla Semi, Model Y, and Model 3 at a demo in Texas.

items.title: When it came to Cal AI's viral success, a small army of influencers paid off
items.snippet: The company generated over $30 million in revenue in two years and was acquired by MyFitnessPal for an undisclosed amount of money in March.

items.title: And the winner of Startup Battlefield at Disrupt 2026 is: Intero Biosystems
items.snippet: Intero Biosystems beat out 199 other Startup Battlefield companies to take home the $100,000 grand prize at TechCrunch Disrupt 2026.

items.title: Amazon devices chief Panos Panay on the importance of failure and bouncing back from it

items.title: Google restricts every free AI Pro trial from Pixel & more compared to paid subscribers
items.snippet: Google hands out extended free trials to its AI Pro subscription frequently with new smartphone purchases and more, but trial users end up getting less access compared to paid subscribers in what is a bit of a misleading situation. Free trials are a pretty standard practice across the industry when it comes to subscriptions, and the general understanding is that you’re getting full access to the same subscription you are later set to pay for unless there’s an upfront stipulation about restrictions. And that’s where things are getting a bit messy with Google’s AI Pro subscription. Google One AI Pro is a $19.99/month subscription that delivers access to expanded Gemini usage limits, 5TB of storage across Google products, and bundles in other subscriptions such as Google Home Premium, Health Premium, and YouTube Premium Lite. Earlier this year, we called AI Pro “one of the best deals in tech today.” But the rollout of Gemini 4 Argon to Google’s Antigravity development tool put a spotlight on a restriction on AI Pro’s free trials. Put simply, they’re limited compared to paid subscribers…

items.title: IDC: Apple closes in on Samsung as global smartphone shipments see record decline in Q3
items.snippet: In a report published today, IDC says Apple saw a 4% year-over-year decline in global iPhone shipments during Q3 2026, but its share of worldwide smartphone shipments increased 23.1% over the same period last year. Here’s why. IDC says its preliminary data on global smartphone shipments for Q3 2026 show a 22% drop compared to Q3 2025, which is in line with other regional and global trends reported recently. The culprit, as even occasional 9to5Mac readers are likely well aware by now, is the ongoing memory shortage, which has sent component costs soaring and squeezed device manufacturers, particularly those competing in lower-end markets. According to IDC, Samsung remained atop the ranking with 57.8 million units shipped and a 22.6% share, down 5.8% from the year-ago period. Apple came in second with 57.3 million shipped units, followed by Xiaomi, OPPO, and vivo. items.title: Today in Apple history: Former CEO John Sculley bids Apple a $10 million farewell
items.snippet: October 15, 1993: John Sculley, the former CEO responsible for forcing Steve Jobs out of Apple, is forced to leave the company himself. When Sculley resigns as Apple’s chairman, he leaves with a golden parachute. His parting gifts include $1 million in severance pay, a one-year consulting fee of $750,000, a commitment from Apple to buy his $4 million mansion and $2 million Learjet, and $2.4 million in stock options. Total take: around $10 million. John Sculley came to Apple to help Steve Jobs change the world. A decade later, he exited a company in crisis with a multimillion-dollar farewell package in tow. The former Pepsi-Cola Company executive famously helped push Jobs out in 1985, then presided over Apple’s rise into a multibillion-dollar business — and its slide toward the turmoil of the 1990s. Sculley resignation on this day in 1993 ended one of the most consequential and controversial chapters in Apple’s history. But his departure was more than the end of a CEO’s run. It was another reminder that the man who helped build Apple’s corporate future also set the stage for its grea…

This refurbished 2018 MacBook Air has a 13-inch Retina display and a grade-A rating, and it’s on sale for $267.99. The coolest part? It comes in a unique, sleek gold color. A 1.6GHz dual-core Intel Core i5 turbo-boosts to 3.6GHz, enough for browsing, document editing, and light photo editing. With 8GB of RAM, you can keep a browser and a few apps open while you work. Storage is a 256GB SSD. On the 13.3-inch Retina display, a 2560×1600 resolution keeps text and photos sharp.

items.title: Best iPhone 2026: Every iPhone compared
items.snippet: Macworld Apple’s 2026 iPhone lineup is broader than ever, ranging from the relatively affordable iPhone 17e to the high-end iPhone 18 Pro and Pro Max , plus the ultra-thin iPhone Air and the new folding iPhone Duo . That gives buyers more choice, but it also makes picking the right model more complicated than simply choosing the newest or most expensive iPhone. items.snippet: Macworld The touchscreen MacBook is reportedly going to be a reality very soon ( October 28 , apparently), and one of the questions about the new way to interface with the Mac is how macOS will accommodate our fingers. items.snippet: Macworld The touchscreen MacBook Pro has been the subject of speculation ever since Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman first reported in 2023 that Apple was exploring the idea. items.title: HomeView quickly won a place in my heart—and my home
items.snippet: Macworld Apple has taken its sweet time to make a smart display – just as it didn’t rush to make a folding phone. Google and Amazon have been in the smart display business for the best part of a decade, while Apple fans have been watching from the sidelines, with a HomePod in the corner of their kitchen and an iPad propped against the toaster. items.title: OPC Global Summit: News spans AI-optimized hardware, cooling equipment
items.snippet: The OCP Global Summit is taking place this week in San Jose, Calif., and the news is flowing. The summit is an annual conference of the Open Compute Project , an industry initiative focused on developing more open, efficient, and scalable hardware designs for data centers and other computing infrastructure. The summit covers the physical infrastructure behind cloud computing and AI data centers, including AI servers and accelerators, standardized or openly-shared designs for hardware, power and cooling, and networking and connectivity. items.title: Ultra Ethernet 1.1 extends the specification to scale-up networks and adds programmable congestion control
items.snippet: The Ultra Ethernet Consortium (UEC) is pushing forward to meet evolving networking needs with the release of UEC 1.1 on October 12. The UEC got its start in 2023 to help improve Ethernet for the growing needs of AI and high-performance computing (HPC) networks. The consortium published its 1.0 specification in June 2025. That release defined a transport protocol, congestion control mechanisms and a modern remote direct memory access (RDMA) approach. With UEC 1.1 , the specification is adding scale-up support, in-network collectives, and programmable congestion control. Specifically, the improvements in UEC 1.1 include: Scale-up networks.
